problem:
What is the variance of the following data set?

$$
9,\,13,\,2,\,14,\,7
$$

Do not round your answer.

${\sigma }^{2}=$
{{field-1}}
worked_solution:
If we have a data set that consists of the points ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n},$ then the variance can be computed as

$$
{\sigma }^{2}=\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2},
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}$ is the mean of the data set and $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}$ is the mean of the squares of the points in the data set.

First, let's compute $\overset{―}{x}.$ There are $n=5$ points in our data set, so the mean is

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{x} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (9+13+2+14+7) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 45 \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's compute $\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}.$ Computing the mean of the squares of the points in the data set, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{―}{{x}^{2}} & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot ({9}^{2}+{13}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{14}^{2}+{7}^{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot (81+169+4+196+49) \\  & =\frac{1}{5}\cdot 499 \\  & =\frac{499}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sigma }^{2} & =\overset{―}{{x}^{2}}-(\overset{―}{x})^{2} \\  & =\frac{499}{5}-{(9)}^{2} \\  & =\frac{499}{5}-81 \\  & =\frac{499-405}{5} \\  & =\frac{94}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
